newsitem.title: UK: S.Africa's Sigcau says SAA needs strong partner.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Sigcau says SAA needs strong partner.

text.p: South African Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said on Tuesday national carrier South African Airways must find a partner with strong management and the necessary financing and technology to operate in an increasingly competitive environment.

"There is a lot of competition and if SAA continues alone and does not bring in a partner with good managerial skills, the necessary finance and technology, it might not really be able to see itself running very well into the future," she told a news conference.
She said the restructuring of SAA would be completed during 1998. The sale of a strategic equity stake in SAA was expected in 1998.
Sigcau added that there was interest in the airline despite the fact that it registered a loss in the 1996/7 financial year.
She said SAA's first priority was to separate from Transnet, the state transport firm which owns SAA.
Also, Sigcau said the tender process for the sale of 100 percent of Sun Air is underway and that a shortlist was due to be announced soon.
Sigcau said she was not in a position to name the parties on the shortlist, but further details could be released later on Tuesday.

She said a 49 percent stake in Sun Air would likely be sold to a foreign airline, 25 percent to black empowerment groups associated with the airline, six percent to an employee share option plan and the National Empowerment Fund 20 percent.

She would not give a figure on the proceeds that would be generated from the country's privatisation effort but said: "We are trying to make sure that we don't sell our entities as if it is a fire sale."
